title: 2026 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: The integers from \(1\) through \(25\) are arbitrarily separated into five groups of \(5\) numbers each. The median of each group is identified. Let \(M\) equal the median of the five medians. What is the least possible value of \(M?\)

solutions.text: If a group has median at most \(8\), then at least \(3\) numbers in that group are at most \(8\). For the median of the five medians to be at most \(8\), at least \(3\) groups would need such medians, requiring at least \(9\) numbers at most \(8\), impossible. Thus \(M\ge9\). This is attainable, for example with group medians \(5,8,9,12,17\): use groups \(\{3,4,5,20,21\}\), \(\{6,7,8,22,23\}\), \(\{1,2,9,24,25\}\), \(\{10,11,12,13,14\}\), and \(\{15,16,17,18,19\}\). Hence the least possible value is \(9\).
hints: A group median at most \(m\) needs at least \(3\) numbers at most \(m\)
Three small medians would require too many small numbers
